hook: The cognitive load of tasks you haven't done is higher than the load of doing them.
topic: The mental cost of the backlog — cognitive overhead from avoided tasks
body:
**The cognitive load of every task you haven't done is higher than the cognitive load of actually doing them. Your backlog is not neutral. It is costing you performance every single day.**

Every unfinished, deferred, or avoided task stays open in what psychologists call an open loop — an active background process your brain is running in parallel with whatever you're trying to focus on. The more open loops you have, the less processing capacity you have available for the work in front of you.

This is why, on days when your backlog is long, everything feels harder. Your focus is fractured not by external distractions, but by internal ones — the constant low-level awareness of what's not done.

The list isn't a productivity tool if it's full of items you're not going to do. It's a stress delivery system.

The reframe: clearing your backlog is not an administrative task. It is the single highest-leverage cognitive performance action available to you, because it restores the processing capacity everything else depends on.

One action: spend fifteen minutes today doing a brain dump — everything unfinished, deferred, or nagging. Then delete or delegate anything that isn't actually yours to do. Close the loops or kill them.
